holes_found.description: The re-run rule is mechanical for the DR-1 labels, but not for the rest of the file (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20261019T004500.json:stamp_preconditions.definitive_data_rerun_rule). (a) label_table covers only the DR-1 as-if labels and two Z quantities. It leaves out every pre-registered and site-registered outcome that also depends on the magnetic data: OBS-D-02/03/04, OBS-O-01/02/03, B2-M-001, B2-M-002, E-PRED-B, the WIN-010 profile result, the Tier-1 r > 0.5 clause, the card's own falsifier on R1, and the dome's BOU quiet test. A definitive re-run that flipped one of those would not count as "material" under the rule. This is not hypothetical. B2-M-002 is "unevaluable as registered" partly because GUI is excluded under DQ-1 for a 185 nT publication-state step in its baseline (criteria.OBS_O_01.detail). Definitive data are the very thing that should remove that step, which could make GUI evaluable and change B2-M-002 and OBS-O-01. (b) material_definition only tests "crosses 3 (SD) or 0.8 (power)". Several listed numbers are neither: the a80 falsified-portion bounds (nT), card R1 raw H (nT), and SPT R2 with its in-band flag (boolean). So the rule cannot say whether a change in them matters. In particular, the disclosed dome-favourable reading (R2 inside the formula band) could flip either way without counting as material. (c) The trigger lists EBR/SPT, the 8 Z-joint stations and ASC/KOU/HER, but not BOU. The headline and both notes state the dome's BOU quiet-test failure (7.62 vs < 5 nT; "no day of July-August 2026 passed it"), and the 2026 BOU files are best-available too. (d) Minor: the matched/mismatched and 60-min entries give only "rev5_lag_joint.json:summary". The exact keys are kappa1.672|admissible_lag_le_30|any_template.min (2.52), kappa1.672|all_lags_0_60|lag_matched_template.min (2.87) and kappa1.672|all_lags_0_60|any_template.min (1.21).
holes_found.recommendation: (a) Extend label_table with one row per data-dependent registered outcome, each with its draft path and today's value: criteria.OBS_D_02..04 and OBS_O_01..03 result/as_if, registered_prediction_scorecard.B2-M-001/B2-M-002.result, site_registered_tests.E_PRED_B.result and WIN_010_profile.scored_result, PRED_TIER_1.as_if_DR1.r_gt_0p5_clause, card R1 falsifier fired (no) and the BOU 2026-08-12 Z daily stdev (7.62, label rule "quiet test failed while >= 5 nT"). Where a row comes from build_* logic rather than a JSON output, name the script and key. (b) Give every numbers_to_compare entry its own criterion, or tag it "report-only". Suggested: any boolean or band-membership flips (R2 in formula band; R1 in falsifier band; R1 in claim band); a80 bounds report-only unless the label changes; nT readings report-only. (c) Add BOU to the trigger list. Add one line on DQ-1: if definitive data remove GUI's publication-state step, DQ-1 no longer excludes GUI, and any criterion that changes as a result is material. (d) Use exact summary keys. Text only; no script changes.

holes_found.description: Kim & Chang 2018: Erratum 1 E-2 misreads the source, and rev6 carries the stale status forward. E-2 (predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-erratum-2026-09-27.json:entries[E-2].unverified_attributions) says the ASR abstract "describes about 207 data sets from 100 INTERMAGNET observatories over 1991-2016 and does not state an eclipse count". Those are the words of the OTHER 2018 Kim & Chang paper, J. Korean Astron. Soc. 51(4):119-127, doi 10.5303/JKAS.2018.51.4.119. I read its abstract this run (koreascience.or.kr via doi.org): "We analyze an average of the 207 geomagnetic field variation data sets observed by 100 INTERMAGNET geomagnetic nodes, during the period from 1991 to 2016", with no eclipse count. The same abstract is the source of the "increase in the Y component and decreases in the X, Z and F components", the magnitude dependence and the 30-50 deg magnetic-latitude band. The ASR abstract (doi 10.1016/j.asr.2018.01.022) states "207 geomagnetic manifestations acquired by 100 geomagnetic observatories during 39 solar eclipses occurring from 1991 to 2016". That was verified in the ISS-3113 c1 review; I could not re-read it this run, because the Elsevier landing page only redirects and Crossref, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar carry no abstract. So the frozen file's "39-eclipse 1991-2016 INTERMAGNET ensemble" description of the ASR paper was right on that point, and E-2 retracted it wrongly. The author/title correction in E-2 stands; Crossref confirms Jung-Hee Kim & Heon-Young Chang, ASR 61(8):2040-2049. Rev6 does not repeat E-2's wording. But honest_limits still says "the \"39-eclipse\" figure and the component pattern remain unverified pending the ISS-3101 full-text check", and site_registered_tests.WIN_010_profile.failure_attribution_note says its basis "is under the ISS-3101 citation review / erratum E-2". Both are stale: ISS-3101 is closed (fixed), and the 39-eclipse figure is verified. Neither says that the latitude band and the Z component come from the JKAS paper. A critic who reads both abstracts can show that our own erratum misread its source, in the very file we are stamping. It does not affect any verdict or label.
holes_found.recommendation: Ship a dated Erratum 2 with the results, stamped in the same OTS batch. Leave Erratum 1 unedited; it is stamped. Erratum 2 should say: (1) E-2's "does not state an eclipse count" is wrong for the ASR paper (its abstract states 39 solar eclipses); the frozen file's ensemble description was right on that point; the author/title correction stands. (2) E-2 quoted the abstract of a second paper, Kim & Chang 2018 JKAS 51(4):119-127, doi 10.5303/JKAS.2018.51.4.119. That paper is the source of the X/Z/F-decrease, Y-increase pattern, the magnitude dependence and the 30-50 deg magnetic-latitude band. (3) Map each of our frozen uses to its paper: the B1-M-001 range basis, the WIN-010 binary latitude profile, and any pattern clause. (4) failure_attribution: analyst_representation (an error in our erratum). Then in rev7, replace the honest_limits line and the WIN_010_profile.failure_attribution_note pointer with a pointer to Erratum 2, and drop "unverified pending ISS-3101". Decider: ISS-3101 was closed against E-2; open a fresh issue rather than reopening it. The ISS-3113 c1 follow-up (JKAS vs ASR attribution on WIN-010/WIN-068/pre-registration) covers the site surfaces; this hole covers the results and erratum files. Side note, no action: the dome's own Tier-1 pattern clause (03-predictions.txt:109, "Y up, X/Z/F down matching Kim & Chang 2018 ensemble") also matches the JKAS abstract, not the ASR one.

holes_found.description: The rule text calls the card's gate point "the registration's most testable claimed amplitude (card: -17.8 nT)" (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20261019T004500.json:symmetric_evaluation_rules.DR-1_detectability_override.rev6_unified_standard). -17.8 is the card's central value. Its most testable claimed amplitude is the band floor, -19.8. Our band is gated at its floor (-25). The difference is outcome-neutral: in every card-admissible variant a80 is -9.25 to -12.75 nT, so the whole stated band and the whole formula band have power >= 0.8. Only our band gets a reported "falsified portion"; the card does not. Saying in one sentence that the card's portion would be the whole band would pre-empt a defender's "you gated us differently". Also, DR-1.text (defined 2026-09-27) still says a claim is scored "ONLY for the part of its predicted amplitude that exceeds 3 x the empirical null SD". Rev6 now bounds the falsified part by a80, a stricter boundary. rev6_unified_standard says so, but DR-1.text carries no pointer to it.
holes_found.recommendation: rev6_unified_standard: "(card: its claimed value -17.8 nT; its whole stated and formula bands lie inside the 0.8-power region in every admissible variant, a80 -9.25 to -12.75 nT, so its falsified portion is the whole band)". Append to DR-1.text, or add a note beside it: "Operationally superseded for the falsified-portion boundary by rev6_unified_standard (0.8-power amplitude a80)." Leave the original text unedited.

deeper_analysis: Other side, argued: (1) "Gating our band at -25 nT but the card at -17.8 is a double standard." Each registration is gated at the amplitude it claims, and the card's whole band is in the 0.8-power region anyway, so the choice cannot have changed the card's label (C6-4 asks for that sentence). (2) "Calling your own ESK/LER UNTESTED is self-serving." It follows mechanically from the gate the rule already stated, which was applied to the card first; this review reproduced the LER/ESK powers independently. Under the no-gate alternative the card label is the same, and the draft says so. (3) "Your re-run rule lets you ignore a definitive-data flip on the criteria you got wrong." As written, partly yes; hence C6-1. (4) In the other direction, a careful critic could say the erratum process cannot be trusted if Erratum 1 misread its source; hence C6-2, and the answer is to correct it in the open. Severity: none of C6-1..C6-4 changes a number, a label or a headline verdict. C6-1 and C6-2 change what the stamped file promises or says about our own sources, which is why they are moderate rather than minor.
